messages:

Cc: carlos.mendes@finassist.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — started 09:08 PT

Kimberly,

We started seeing a user-facing error spike at ~09:08 PT right after your team’s morning deploy. End users are getting timeouts and 429 spam; our API error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 18% and overall request latency doubled. Attached is a short log snippet and a screenshot from our dashboard showing the spike.

Impact: automated lending decision flow failing for ~15% of requests (real-time path). This is affecting several key customers on our platform; SLAs are being hit.

Can you confirm: did Redwood push a new quantization/profile or kernel change for model-v12 this morning? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA. We have a support line ready for a bridge if you can spin one up.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Director, Product Ops — FinAssist

Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — started 09:08 PT

Sofia — thank you for the alert and for the logs. I’m on it.

Short summary from our side: today at 08:55 PT we completed a canary rollout of model-v12 with a new quantization profile and a revised kernel selection heuristic on the serving cluster that handles your routing. Canary passed locally but we did not see this traffic shape in staging.

Immediate plan (30m):
- Start bridge now (I’ve invited infra & runtime): 09:25 PT bridge URL in the next message.
- Roll routing back to model-v11 for FinAssist traffic only (force variant) — target: 09:30 PT.
- Temporarily disable continuous-batching on FinAssist routes and cap batch_size to 1.
- If rollback reduces errors we will keep v11 pinned and run a targeted investigation.

I’ll kick off the rollback and post updates here. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize fixes and a post-mortem.

Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-checklist.pdf

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — started 09:08 PT

On it — short diagnostic notes from the runtime team:

Observations so far (09:24 PT):
- Error pattern: mixture of 5xx (internal server error / OOM) and 429 rate-limit-style failures. 429s are coming from our local request queue overflow, not upstream rate-limiter: implies retry amplification / long tails.
- Deployment delta: quant profile reduced model weights to int8 and the compilation chose a new kernel variant for the attention blocks; memory footprint per-request decreased in synthetic tests but we’re seeing increased kernel exec time for some long-context requests leading to backlog.
- Hypothesis: longer kernel latency + unadjusted batching resulted in queue buildup; clients retried aggressively causing 429s; some instances hit OOM when KV cache allocation patterns changed for model-v12.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:28 PT:
- Forced FinAssist routing to model-v11 (completed 09:30 PT).
- Disabled continuous-batching on those routes and set max_batch_size=1 (09:31 PT).
- Hot patch to increase request-queue capacity on affected pool (09:33 PT).

Preliminary telemetry (09:40 PT): error-rate down from 18% -> 2.1% for FinAssist; latency trending back toward baseline. Not fully healed but improving.

Next steps:
- Collect kernel exec profiles for the affected requests and compare timing distributions between v11 and v12 (running now).
- If kernel inefficiency confirmed: revert kernel heuristic for v12 and re-run canary with smaller batch footprint.
- Longer term: add a pre-deploy perf gate that replays customer-shaped traces.

Attaching kernel-alloc.log excerpt and brief profile note.

—Aditya
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kernel-alloc.log

Folks — short executive summary for visibility and approval:

What happened:
- Canary of model-v12 with a new quant profile and kernel heuristic caused a production degradation surface for FinAssist starting 09:08 PT. The runtime changes caused queue amplification and some OOMs on the serving pool referenced below.
- Immediate rollback to v11 for FinAssist traffic completed 09:30 PT; mitigation actions reduced error rate to ~2% by 09:40 PT and latency is returning to normal.

Customer impact:
- FinAssist reported ~15% of real-time decision requests affected at peak. They are a large account in our Financial vertical (volume-sensitive). They are asking for an incident bridge and an explanation within the day; they also asked about credits.

Recommendation & asks:
- Approve issuing a one-time service credit of 40% for the affected window (09:08–09:40 PT) to FinAssist as a gesture of goodwill.
- Approve an immediate customer-only post-mortem and a technical write-up of root cause for FinAssist by EOD Monday.
- Prioritize a perf gate (replay of customer traces) as a P1 for runtime over the next sprint.

If approved I’ll coordinate comms and the credit. Please reply with approval or suggested changes.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success (Prod Escalations)
Redwood Inference

Sofia / Carlos — closing the loop for today.

Status: rollback to model-v11 for your traffic completed at 09:30 PT and we observed error rate return to near baseline by 09:40 PT. Our telemetry shows the affected serving pool saw a transient queue amplification due to the new kernel execution time distribution on v12.

Action items and timeline:
- Root cause: kernel selection + quant profile combination caused longer per-request kernel execs for some long-context requests; this pushed the queue into long tails and amplified retries.
- Immediate: v11 pinned for FinAssist; continuous-batching disabled for your routes; we increased queue capacity temporarily.
- Next week: aditya/ runtime will produce a detailed kernel profile and proposed kernel heuristic rollback for v12 (ETA Tue 11/16). PM/CS will provide a customer-facing post-mortem and proposed credit (Marissa to handle).

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. We value FinAssist’s partnership and will run a follow-up call Monday to walk through the findings. Please let me know if you want an earlier bridge.

Thanks for your patience,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
